findings.evidence: It had been true enough when she started.
findings.diagnosis: The narration adjudicates the moral status of the kind lie — the story's own question surfacing in free-indirect narration; the flagged two-hander risk.

findings.evidence: It was the thing she had instead of the thing Mam had always handed him for nothing.
findings.diagnosis: The old wound stated as aphorism; the meaning handed to the reader rather than dramatized in a concrete fact.

findings.evidence: Lena was through the search and stamped and sitting on the bolted chairs by ten past
findings.diagnosis: The search and rules of the hall — the mechanics the contract asks to carry the feeling — are summarized away in a clause. (Its genuine advantage over candidate-a: it DOES plant the lie on the page — 'Mam sends her love' — which arms the ending.)

findings.evidence: held it the rest of the way like a cup she didn't want to spill.
findings.diagnosis: More writerly than dry report; pre-echoes the literal tea a touch too neatly.
